title: Human languages are gaining share
author: curious-geeks-round2
hypothesis: Titles matching the linguistics, translation or Unicode word list take at least 1.25x as much of the story mix in the final three complete weeks as in the first three.
expect: Support at ratio 1.25x or above; refute at 1.0x or below; between those thresholds is inconclusive. Compare equal-weight complete-week rates, not pooled totals.
caveats: Definitions and thresholds saved before this aggregation, but earlier project summaries were already inspected. Exploratory, not blind or independently preregistered, and not a statistical significance test.

Title proxy only; the exact regex is \b(linguist\w*|etymolog\w*|dialects?|bilingual|multilingual|translation|translate|phonetic\w*|alphabets?|unicode)\b. Matches can overlap themes and can be ambiguous (for example, software libraries are also books matches).
70,571 eligible live stories in 10 complete UTC weeks, July 27 through October 4, 2026. No comments, jobs, dead or deleted items. Only manifest-listed chunks are read.
Scores and comment counts are snapshots, with unequal age and collection timing; current updates do not refresh older scores. Associations do not establish what causes attention.
Missing scores/comments are excluded from their denominators; comments-per-point uses only stories with both fields. Each plotted row is a rate; the verdict averages rates equally.
Three early and three late weeks only; short-term fluctuation is not a durable adoption trend. All ten weeks are graphed for context.
151 matching stories across the window. Small weekly groups can have unstable rates. These 15 checks have no multiplicity correction; supported means only the descriptive threshold was crossed.
